title: Values and loops in Swift
summary: Use an array, a filtered loop, and an explicit return type to count positives.

scenario.briefing: A campus app summarizes stock changes. Count positive changes in Swift without hiding the result type.

objectives.description: Apply the taught syntax in a working file.
Count positives in a new array with filter and count.

misconceptions.description: Counting zero as a positive change.
misconceptions.testDescription: The loop counts only positive values.
misconceptions.feedback: Zero is not positive. The condition must be value > 0, not value >= 0.

misconceptions.description: Declaring the counter with let and trying to increment it.
misconceptions.diagnostic: Declaring count with let, then assigning count += 1 inside the loop.
misconceptions.feedback: let creates a constant. A counter that changes needs var.

misconceptions.description: Believing force unwrapping is safe after an optional check.
misconceptions.feedback: Force unwrapping traps when the optional is nil. Use if let or guard let so the compiler proves the value exists.

misconceptions.description: Counting every array element instead of the filtered ones.
misconceptions.feedback: count on the filtered array counts only positives. Counting the original array includes zero and negatives.

sections.title: Swift values and decisions
sections.body: Swift declares constants with let count = 3 and variables with var total = 0. Type inference keeps the declaration concise. An optional Int? either contains an Int or nil. if let, guard let, and optional chaining make absence explicit. if and switch select branches, and switch must be exhaustive. A for loop visits a collection: for value in values { ... }.

steps.title: Filter and count
steps.prompt: Given let values = [4, 0, -3, 7], what does values.filter { $0 > 0 }.count return?
hints: filter keeps elements that satisfy the closure.
The negative value does not satisfy it either.

quiz.prompt: Given let values = [4, 0, -3, 7], what does values.filter { $0 > 0 }.count return?

options.label: 4, because count uses the original array
0, because filter returns an empty array

quiz.explanation: filter keeps 4 and 7, so the resulting array has two elements. count reports that array's length.
